description: Eight confirmed observed images with individual Commons provenance: pollination, tree roots, diatom, elephant herd, rice harvesting, industrial flywheel, petroglyph heritage and habitat restoration.

images.title: A bumblebee among the flowers
images.summary: A macro photograph shows a furry bee foraging among the pollen-bearing structures of a magenta zinnia in Pennsylvania in 2023.
images.alt: Close-up of a black and pale yellow fuzzy bee standing on the yellow center of a vivid magenta zinnia blossom.
images.caption: Flowering plants and insects often exchange food and pollen. This photograph shows a bee visiting a zinnia; pollen transfer between flowers was not directly observed.
images.rights: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication, as stated on the individual Wikimedia Commons file page. Photographer credited as provenance.
images.processing: Source image resized to maximum side 1800px and re-encoded as quality-87 JPEG for development archive, without synthesizing or adding content; original source URL retained.

images.title: Buttress roots in a Western Ghats forest
images.summary: A tree in the evergreen Western Ghats of India shows large, flared buttress roots extending from the base of its trunk.
images.alt: Wide fluted green-gray roots rise from damp brown leaf litter and converge at the broad base of a rainforest tree.
images.caption: The base of a living tree displays its outward-spreading support structures. The full forest canopy and underground root system are not visible.
images.rights: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication, as stated on the individual Wikimedia Commons file page. Photographer credited as provenance.
images.processing: Source image resized to maximum side 1800px and re-encoded as quality-87 JPEG for development archive, without synthesizing or adding content; original source URL retained.

images.title: A marine diatom at microscopic scale
images.summary: An observational photomicrograph of a star-stick diatom acquired by John R. Dolan for the NOAA Photo Library, with a 50-micrometer scale bar.
images.alt: Transparent elongated diatom cell with patterned yellow-orange star-shaped structures against slate-blue microscope field and 50-micrometer scale marker.
images.caption: Diatoms are photosynthetic single-celled algae and important members of marine phytoplankton. This image shows one diatom, not the entire marine food web.
images.credit: John R. Dolan / NOAA Photo Library
images.rights: Public-domain NOAA official-duty photograph in the United States. Commons also records an earlier Flickr CC BY 2.0 mark and notes its uncertain applicability; author and NOAA credit retained.
images.processing: Source image resized to maximum side 1800px and re-encoded as quality-87 JPEG for development archive, without synthesizing or adding content; original source URL retained.

images.title: Elephants gather in the Ugandan savannah
images.summary: Elephants shelter under a large tree in Kidepo Valley National Park in northern Uganda, within a broad grassland and woodland landscape.
images.alt: Several African elephants gather beneath the canopy of a large savannah tree amid open golden grass and scattered trees.
images.caption: A group of elephants in their savannah ecosystem. Other mammals and ecosystems are not shown in this single frame.
images.rights: CC BY-SA 4.0 International (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/). Original photo by Chapelle Musa 2; 1280px Commons derivative locally resized and re-encoded; derivative licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.
images.processing: Uses Wikimedia Commons 1280-pixel thumbnail (the 29.65 MB source master remains on Commons), re-encoded at quality 87 for local archive; no content additions.

images.title: People and machines harvest rice
images.summary: At a family farm near El Campo, Texas, agricultural machinery harvests rice while workers move crops and coordinate the work, photographed July 2020.
images.alt: Large green agricultural harvester moves through golden rice with tractor and grain trailer further behind on the same broad field.
images.caption: Modern mechanical crop harvesting helps humans produce and distribute food. This is a specific contemporary Texas rice farm, not a universal representation of agriculture.
images.credit: Lance Cheung / USDA Natural Resources Conservation Service
images.rights: U.S. Department of Agriculture federal employee photograph, public domain in the United States; credit Lance Cheung / USDA.
images.processing: Source image resized to maximum side 1800px and re-encoded as quality-87 JPEG for development archive, without synthesizing or adding content; original source URL retained.

images.title: An industrial engine's flywheel
images.summary: A stationary steam engine's cylinder and flywheel in the Deutsches Museum, Munich, photographed in 2024. The flywheel smooths variations in rotational motion.
images.alt: Large historic steam machinery with a broad dark metal flywheel and cylinder visible in a museum hall.
images.caption: Stationary steam-engine technology converted heat energy into mechanical rotation. A flywheel stores kinetic energy and smooths the output cycle.
images.rights: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication, as stated on the individual Wikimedia Commons file page. Photographer credited as provenance.
images.processing: Source image resized to maximum side 1800px and re-encoded as quality-87 JPEG for development archive, without synthesizing or adding content; original source URL retained.

images.title: Petroglyph at Puako, Hawaiʻi
images.summary: An engraved lava-rock petroglyph at the Puako Petroglyph Archaeological District on Hawaiʻi Island, photographed in 2011.
images.alt: Incised symbolic lines cut into a dark porous volcanic rock, surrounded by pebbles and dry vegetation.
images.caption: A historic Hawaiian rock engraving. Its makers' intended meanings and chronology are not established by the photo alone; respect for indigenous cultural interpretation remains important.
images.rights: Photographic representation licensed CC0 1.0 by Wmpearl. This license concerns the photograph, not ownership of underlying Native Hawaiian cultural heritage or interpretation; cultural review pending.
images.processing: Source image resized to maximum side 1800px and re-encoded as quality-87 JPEG for development archive, without synthesizing or adding content; original source URL retained.

images.title: Hands-on habitat restoration
images.summary: United States Fish and Wildlife Service staff and partner volunteers planted roughly 300 native plants as part of a stream-restoration project in southern California in 2018.
images.alt: One man kneels by newly planted shrubs and earth as another worker in high-visibility clothing digs in the background.
images.caption: A cooperative native-plant restoration project carried out by conservation teams and local partners, illustrating active human stewardship of a landscape.
images.credit: Jonathan Snapp-Cook / U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service
images.rights: Official-duty US Fish and Wildlife Service photograph, public domain in United States; photographer Jonathan Snapp-Cook credited.
